Courses.Title: Prin of Financial Accounting
Courses.Description: Designed for all business majors to introduce the core concepts of financial accounting and a complete overview of financial statement reporting.

Courses.Title: Prin of Managerial Accounting
Courses.Description: Designed for all business majors to introduce the core concepts of managerial accounting and a complete overview of managerial planning, budgeting, analysis and decision making.

Courses.Title: Intermediate Accounting I
Courses.Description: This is the first of a two-course series tailored for accounting and finance majors. It comprehensively explores Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and the reporting requirements established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB).

Courses.Title: Intermediate Accounting II
Courses.Description: This is the second course of a two-course series tailored for accounting and finance majors. It comprehensively explores Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and the reporting requirements established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB).

Courses.Title: Taxation I
Courses.Description: An in-depth examination of the taxation of individuals; an introduction to the basic concepts underlying the taxation system, including its structure and administration; and an introduction to basic tax research sources and techniques.

Courses.Title: Advanced Financial Accounting
Courses.Description: Understanding leases, pensions, and postretirement benefits, the equity method of accounting for investments, consolidation of financial statements, variable interest entities, partnerships, state and local governments, and not-for-profit entities.

Courses.Title: Auditing
Courses.Description: The capstone accounting course and the first of two courses designed for an in-depth examination of audit and assurance services for both public and private entities.

Courses.Title: Accounting Internship
Courses.Description: Designed for undergraduate accounting majors pursuing full-time, paid internships that are pre-approved and monitored by accounting faculty. A total of 75 work hours is required for each credit hour. Part-time internships must meet the same approval and monitoring requirements and will receive 1 or 2 credit hours depending upon the number of work hours required.
